OCCUPATIONAL HEALTH & SAFETY

Safe work is
the only work.

Global Mino’s OHS approach is built for gold mining, mineral exploration and remote field operations—protecting employees, contractors, visitors and neighbouring communities through planned controls, clear accountability and readiness to respond.

OUR COMMITMENT

Everyone goes to work
with the right to return safe.

Our objective is to prevent injury and work-related ill health by planning safe work, consulting the people who perform it and acting when conditions are unsafe.

The same expectations extend to employees, contractors and visitors. Site controls also consider traffic, dust, water, blasting, access and emergency scenarios that could affect surrounding communities.

Stop-work authorityVisible leadershipWorker consultationNo retaliation for reporting

OHS POLICY

Principles that guide
every operating decision.

Leadership & accountability

Managers define responsibilities, provide resources and verify critical controls. Supervisors confirm work is understood before it starts; every individual remains responsible for following controls and raising concerns.

Risk before task

Baseline assessments, task risk reviews and pre-start checks identify hazards, affected people and credible worst-case outcomes before work is authorised.

Fit for work

Fitness, fatigue, heat strain, exposure and wellbeing are considered alongside task capability, with personal health information handled confidentially.

Inclusive protection

Inductions, permits, traffic plans, exclusion zones and emergency information apply to employees, contractors and visitors; off-site impacts are considered for neighbouring communities.

RISK ASSESSMENT & HAZARD IDENTIFICATION

See the risk.
Set the control.
Check it holds.

Risk management begins before mobilisation and continues as ground, weather, people and equipment change. Controls follow the hierarchy: eliminate the hazard where practicable, then substitute, engineer, administrate and use PPE for remaining exposure.

  1. 01IdentifyPeople, task, energy and environment
  2. 02AssessLikelihood, consequence and exposure
  3. 03ControlPrioritise higher-order controls
  4. 04CommunicateBrief, authorise and confirm understanding
  5. 05VerifyInspect critical controls in the field
  6. 06ImproveLearn from work, change and events
STOP WORK

Anyone should pause a task when controls are absent, conditions change or the work is not understood. Work resumes only after the risk is reassessed and controls are restored.

MINING SITE SAFETY

Critical controls
where energy is highest.

Mining hazards can have severe consequences. The operating focus is on controlling interactions between people, vehicles, unstable ground, machinery, electricity, explosives and process materials.

Mobile equipment & traffic

Separate people and vehicles through traffic plans, designated walkways, positive communication, speed controls, lighting, berms and exclusion zones. Seat belts and pre-start inspections are mandatory expectations.

Ground control & excavations

Inspect benches, faces, highwalls, stockpiles, trenches and access routes. Establish stand-off distances, edge protection and barricades, and reassess after rain, blasting or visible change.

Energy isolation

Identify every energy source before maintenance. Isolation, lockout, verification and controlled return to service are completed by authorised, competent people.

Processing & hazardous materials

Guard moving parts, control stored energy, maintain ventilation and manage chemicals through labels, safety data, compatible storage, spill controls and task-specific protection.

Mining equipment safety

  • Competent, authorised operators
  • Documented pre-start inspections
  • Guarding and safety devices
  • Defect isolation and escalation
  • Planned maintenance controls
  • Pedestrian–vehicle separation

EXPLORATION & FIELD SAFETY

Prepared beyond
the last paved road.

Remote exploration requires the same discipline as an operating mine, with added attention to isolation, travel and delayed access to care.

  • Journey managementRoute, driver, vehicle, weather, check-in schedule and overdue action agreed before departure.
  • Remote communicationsPrimary and backup communication, tested coverage and location-sharing appropriate to the work.
  • Field hazardsTerrain, heat, lightning, wildlife, water, manual handling, sampling tools and community access assessed daily.
  • Buddy systemNo isolated work without an approved lone-work control and reliable escalation method.

PERSONAL PROTECTIVE EQUIPMENT

The last line of defence.
Never the first plan.

PPE is selected from the task and exposure assessment, provided in suitable sizes, inspected before use and replaced when damaged. Training covers fit, limitations, cleaning and storage.

01

Core site PPE

Hard hat, safety eyewear, high-visibility clothing and protective footwear where site rules require them.

02

Exposure-specific PPE

Hearing, respiratory, hand, face, fall and chemical protection matched to the identified hazard.

03

Fit & compatibility

Respirator fit and compatibility between multiple items are checked; facial hair and damaged seals are addressed.

04

Visitor controls

Visitors receive an induction, escort and correctly sized PPE before entering controlled operating areas.

EMERGENCY PREPAREDNESS

Ready before
the alarm sounds.

Emergency plans are site-specific, accessible and practiced. Drills test the full chain—from detection and first actions to accountability, communication, evacuation and recovery.

Scenario planning

Plans address credible events such as vehicle incidents, fire, medical emergencies, ground failure, hazardous release, severe weather, security events and missing persons.

On-site response

Alarm methods, trained responders, first-aid resources, rescue capability and incident command are proportionate to site risk and remoteness.

Evacuation & coordination

Muster points, evacuation routes, medevac triggers and contact arrangements with transport providers, receiving facilities and relevant authorities are defined and tested.

DetectRaise alarmStabiliseAccountEscalateRecover

Community interface: Where an operational emergency could extend beyond a site boundary, planning includes warning methods, liaison responsibilities, access controls and coordination with community representatives and public responders.

EMPLOYEE HEALTH & WELLBEING

Protect health across
the full working life.

Occupational health programmes should connect exposure information with confidential health monitoring so early signs of harm can trigger better controls—not blame.

Health risk assessmentDust and silica · noise · vibration · heat · chemicals · ergonomics · biological hazards
Fitness for taskRole demands · work restrictions · fatigue and shift patterns · safe return to work
Health surveillanceRisk-based baseline and periodic checks where exposure indicates a need
Wellbeing supportMental health awareness · hydration · nutrition · fatigue reporting · respectful workplace
ConfidentialityClinical information protected; management receives only fit-for-work guidance and anonymised trends where appropriate

SAFETY TRAINING

Competence is shown
in the field.

Training is role- and risk-based. Understanding is checked through observation, demonstration and supervision—not attendance alone.

01

Induct

Site rules, hazards, emergency actions, reporting and stop-work expectations.

02

Train

Task procedures, permits, equipment, PPE and critical controls for the role.

03

Verify

Competency assessment before unsupervised or safety-critical work.

04

Refresh

Retraining after change, extended absence, an event or identified performance gap.

Every shift starts with context.

Pre-start and toolbox conversations cover today’s work, interactions, changing conditions, lessons from recent events and the controls people must verify.

INCIDENT PREVENTION & REPORTING

Report early.
Learn completely.

Hazards, near misses, injuries, illnesses, spills, equipment damage and community concerns should be reported promptly. Immediate care and scene safety come first; investigations then focus on system causes and control improvement.

A fair, learning-focused culture protects good-faith reporting. Deliberate reckless conduct is handled separately from human error and system weakness.

  1. 01
    Make safeStop, assist and prevent further harm.
  2. 02
    NotifyUse the site escalation route without delay.
  3. 03
    Preserve & understandSecure evidence and involve the people who know the work.
  4. 04
    Correct & shareAssign actions, verify effectiveness and communicate learning.

ENVIRONMENTAL & SITE SAFETY

Safe sites respect
their wider setting.

OHS and environmental controls meet wherever work can affect air, water, land, access or people beyond the immediate task.

Dust & airSuppress, enclose, monitor and maintain separation from receptors.
Water & chemicalsProtect storage, manage spills and keep contaminated flows controlled.
Waste & housekeepingSegregate, contain and remove materials while keeping access and emergency routes clear.
Site securityControl entry, sign hazards and protect visitors and communities from operational areas.
Noise, vibration & blastingPlan, communicate, exclude and monitor in relation to workers and nearby communities.

OHS STANDARDS & COMPLIANCE

Requirements made
visible at the workface.

Before work begins, the applicable legal, regulatory, permit, contractual and site requirements are identified for the country and activity. Responsibilities, records and verification methods are then built into work plans and contractor controls.

Audits and inspections are used to test implementation and close gaps. Requirements are reviewed when legislation, scope, equipment or site conditions change.

Clear statementThis page does not claim that Global Mino holds a particular OHS certification or has achieved a specific safety performance result. Any future certification or numerical performance claim should be published only after independent verification and company approval.

MEASUREMENT & CONTINUOUS IMPROVEMENT

Measure what prevents harm.

Performance review should combine leading indicators with verified event data. Trends are used to prioritise resources, update risk controls and share lessons across projects.

LEADING

Critical controls verified

Field checks confirming the barriers for high-consequence hazards are present and effective.

LEADING

Actions closed effectively

Corrective actions completed on time and checked for sustained effectiveness.

LEADING

Training & competency current

Role requirements completed, assessed and refreshed when conditions change.

HEALTH

Surveillance completed

Risk-based monitoring participation and anonymised trends, handled confidentially.

LEARNING

Hazards & near misses reported

Reporting quality and learning themes—not numerical targets that discourage speaking up.

OUTCOME

Verified incident trends

Severity, exposure and recurrence reviewed only from validated operational data.

No company accident rate, certification status or achievement figure is displayed because verified source data has not been provided.
